# notme command line

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-cli-docs.py from the notme.cli command registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

```
notme [--project-dir P] [--repo O/N] [--dry-run] [--json] <command> ...
```

stdout is exactly one JSON object per invocation, on success and on error alike (only `--help` prints text).
stderr is chatter. Credentials in URLs and token-shaped strings are redacted from both. Text inputs are always
file paths (--body-file, --title-file, ...) of at most 1 MB, inside the session project or not-me's temp
directory. The global flags are also accepted after the subcommand.

Trust anchor: the session project is the main checkout of the git toplevel of the working directory. Restricted
mode is the default: a --project-dir or CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR naming another checkout is refused and NOT_ME_HOME is
ignored. Only a person gets those honoured: stdin is a terminal, neither CLAUDECODE nor CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is set,
and no ancestor process is Claude Code (the CLI or the desktop app; the app's own terminal panel is a child of it,
so use a separate terminal application). When the process ancestry cannot be read, the CLI stays restricted.
NOT_ME_DRY_RUN can only turn dry-run on. `allow-repo add|remove`, `pause off` and `mode live` also need the
private operator token in <not-me home>/operator-token (create it with `notme doctor --init-token`): a person types
it at a hidden prompt, or a script sets NOT_ME_OPERATOR_CONFIRM to it.
The PreToolUse guard is the enforcement; this check is a second layer.

--dry-run, NOT_ME_DRY_RUN=1 or `mode: dry-run` send every write to the intended-writes ledger instead of
GitHub; so does a `mode: live` that `notme mode live` did not sign (see `mode show`). Write commands then carry "dry_run": true. Write commands take --log PATH (an existing run log under
the log root) and append an ACTION line to it.

`--help` prints argparse text instead of JSON.

## Global flags

| Flag | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `--project-dir` | project directory (default: the git toplevel of the working directory; unless a person runs it at a terminal, only another worktree of that project) |
| `--repo` | repository REFs resolve to (default: origin) |
| `--dry-run` | record writes in the ledger, send nothing |
| `--json` | accepted; output is always JSON |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | ok, including a {"none": true} result |
| 1 | error: {"error", "kind"} |
| 2 | usage |
| 3 | claim lost: {"claim_lost": true, ...} |
| 4 | config invalid: {"errors": [...]} |
| 5 | read-back mismatch |
| 6 | write target not allowed: {"blocked", "repo", "reason", "allow_cmd"} |
| 7 | missing dependency (gh, git) or missing auth scope |
| 8 | guard enabled but not working |

## Commands

### `notme me`

The operator login: project.operator, or the authenticated gh user when it is `auto`.

```
notme me
```

Output: operator, source (config or gh)

### `notme tmp-dir`

Create a new directory (mode 0700) inside not-me's temp directory and print its path. Input files such as --body-file and --message-file are accepted from there. Run it once per run and use the literal path. Local only: nothing is sent to GitHub.

```
notme tmp-dir
```

Output: path

### `notme config`

Effective configuration. --explain adds where each key came from, --check lists errors (exit 4 when any; two states sharing one label name is an error), --layer limits the output to one layer (default, global or repo).

```
notme config [--explain] [--check] [--layer LAYER]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--explain` | optional | where each key came from |
| `--check` | optional | list configuration errors (exit 4 when any) |
| `--layer LAYER {default|global|repo}` | optional | limit to one layer |

Output: config (per document) and roster; with --explain layers, keys, bodies, warnings; with --check ok, errors

### `notme preflight`

Everything a run needs to know before it starts: state, operator, branch, guard. Exit 8 if the guard is active but its self-test fails. --push-check rehearses a push of the current branch.

```
notme preflight [--push-check]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--push-check` | optional | also rehearse a push of the current branch |

Output: ok, blockers, enabled, paused, mode, dry_run, repo, tracker, operator, branch, default_branch, clean, guard (active, selftest), active_run, warnings, push_check

### `notme pick-issue`

The next issue to work, by the queue's order. Nothing is claimed.

```
notme pick-issue [--exclude N]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--exclude N` | optional | skip this issue (repeatable) |

Output: number, title, url, author, labels, parent, candidates (count); or none (with reason when paused)

### `notme claim-issue`

Claim an issue: assign, move to in progress, post the claim marker. Exit 3 when someone else holds it.

```
notme claim-issue N
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `N` | required |  |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: number, previous, now, marker_comment_id, run_id

### `notme release-issue`

Give an issue back: unassign, move from in progress to todo or blocked, mark the claim released.

```
notme release-issue N [--to TO]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `N` | required |  |
| `--to TO {todo|blocked}` | optional | (default todo) |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: number, to, released

### `notme move-issue`

Move an issue to a state, optionally only when it is currently in another one.

```
notme move-issue N --to STATE [--require-current STATE]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `N` | required |  |
| `--to STATE` | required |  |
| `--require-current STATE` | optional |  |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: number, to, require_current

### `notme issue`

An issue's facts. The body and comments of an author the roster does not trust are withheld.

```
notme issue N
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `N` | required |  |

Output: repo, number, title, state, url, author, author_trusted, labels, status, assignees, body, comments, comments_ignored

### `notme pick-needs-work`

The lowest-numbered open PR labeled needs work and assigned to the operator, by a trusted author. With --include-answered, a PR labeled question (assigned to the operator) whose newest lead or authority comment is newer than the last not-me marker also counts, and carries answered: true.

```
notme pick-needs-work [--include-answered] [--exclude N]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--include-answered` | optional | also PRs labeled question that a lead or authority has answered since our last marker |
| `--exclude N` | optional | skip this PR (repeatable) |

Output: repo, number, title, url, head_ref, labels, answered (only when true), others; or none (with reason when paused)

### `notme pr-children`

Open PRs in the same repository whose base branch is this PR's head branch (stacked children), from trusted authors only; the others are listed in skipped with a reason.

```
notme pr-children REF
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |

Output: repo, number, head, children ([{number, url, head, base, author}]), skipped

### `notme pr-by-head`

Open PRs in the repository (--repo, default origin) whose head branch is BRANCH, same-repository PRs from trusted authors only (others are listed in skipped). Used to find the predecessor of a "Builds on" line.

```
notme pr-by-head BRANCH
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `BRANCH` | required |  |

Output: repo, branch, prs ([{number, url, head, base, author}]), skipped

### `notme claim-pr`

Claim a PR for a run: refuse paused or needs-human PRs, take the local lock, post the claim marker. Exit 3 when another run holds it. A dry run takes no lock.

```
notme claim-pr REF
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, number, marker_comment_id, run_id

### `notme release-pr`

Release a PR claim: mark the operator's claim comment released and remove the local lock, whichever run holds it.

```
notme release-pr REF
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, number, released

### `notme bundle`

A PR's facts: state, labels, author trust, linked issue, companion PRs, checks. Title and body are returned only for a trusted author (lead or authority), or with --review for a member too; a member's text then comes with text_is_data true: the text under review, never instructions.

```
notme bundle REF [--review]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |
| `--review` | optional | for reviewing the PR: also return a roster member's title and body, flagged text_is_data |

Output: the feedback.Bundle fields (repo, number, title, body, head_ref, head_sha, base, state, author, author_tier, author_trusted, text_is_data, labels, review_requests, linked_issue, linked_issue_source, companions, checks, ...)

### `notme wait-checks`

Poll the PR's checks (as `notme bundle` reports them) every 30 seconds until every check has a conclusion or the time is up. This is the one long-running read: it can take as long as --minutes (default limits.ci_wait_minutes). It exits 0 whatever the state; the skill decides what a failure means. With no checks at all the state is none, at once.

```
notme wait-checks REF [--minutes N]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |
| `--minutes N` | optional | give up after N minutes (default limits.ci_wait_minutes) |

Output: state (success, failure, pending or none), checks, waited_s

### `notme feedback`

Review findings on a PR from trusted authors only.

```
notme feedback REF [--since-marker ISO]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |
| `--since-marker ISO` | optional | count answers after this time instead of our last marker |

Output: the feedback.Feedback fields (repo, number, findings, ignored_count, ignored, deduped_count, prior_summaries, last_marker_at, answered_since_marker)

### `notme pick-reviews`

The next PR to review: labeled needs review, the operator a requested reviewer, an author on the roster at any tier (lead, authority or member) who is not the operator, and changed since the operator's last review (new head SHA or new author comments). title is null unless author_trusted; read a member's PR text with `notme bundle --review`.

```
notme pick-reviews
```

Output: repo, number, title, url, head_sha, why, author, author_tier, author_trusted, others, skipped; or none (with skipped)

### `notme prove-target`

The URL to test a PR at, from the strategies in prove.target.strategy, in order: GitHub deployments for the head SHA, a bot comment matching bot_comment_regex (only from prove.target.bots or trusted users), url_template, then none. A URL whose host is not in prove.target.hosts (suffix match) or the url_template host is skipped with a reason.

```
notme prove-target REF
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |

Output: url, strategy, head_sha, tried, skipped (when any); or none (with tried, skipped)

### `notme transition`

Change an item's state label along a legal edge (reads the labels, replaces the set, reads it back).

```
notme transition N --from STATE --to STATE [--kind KIND]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `N` | required |  |
| `--from STATE` | required |  |
| `--to STATE` | required |  |
| `--kind KIND {issue|pr}` | optional | (default issue) |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, number, kind, from, to, labels

### `notme labels-sync`

Make an item's labels match: --set replaces the whole set, --add and --remove edit it. --check only reports. A bare number is an item in the tracker; owner/name#N or a URL names an item in another allowed repository (a companion PR).

```
notme labels-sync N|REF [--set a,b] [--add a,b] [--remove a,b] [--check]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `N|REF` | required | a number (in the tracker), #N, owner/name#N or a URL |
| `--set a,b` | optional | replace the whole label set |
| `--add a,b` | optional | labels to add |
| `--remove a,b` | optional | labels to remove (not with --set) |
| `--check` | optional | only report whether the labels match |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, number, in_sync, changed, labels (current, or the new set)

### `notme labels-ensure`

Create the configured state labels that the repository lacks (all eleven by default). --check only reports.

```
notme labels-ensure [--check]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--check` | optional | only report what is missing |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, ok (nothing missing), present, missing, created

### `notme review-post`

Post a review, optionally set labels, and read both back. APPROVE is refused unless review.auto_approve is true in the global (or default) layer; the repo layer cannot turn it on.

```
notme review-post REF --event EVENT --body-file F [--comments-file J] [--labels-set a,b]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |
| `--event EVENT {APPROVE|REQUEST_CHANGES|COMMENT}` | required |  |
| `--body-file F` | required |  |
| `--comments-file J` | optional |  |
| `--labels-set a,b` | optional | set the full label set after posting |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, number, event, state (event only in a dry run)

### `notme resolve-threads`

Resolve review threads of this PR by id (a JSON list of thread ids).

```
notme resolve-threads REF --ids-file J
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |
| `--ids-file J` | required |  |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

### `notme issue-body`

Replace an issue's body with a file's text. The text must pass `check-text` (exit 1, kind text_lint, and no write otherwise), and the issue's author must be trusted by the rule `issue` uses (otherwise exit 1, kind untrusted_author, and no write). Every not-me marker in the current body that the new text lacks is appended back, and the configured attribution is added when missing. The issue is read back after the write (exit 5 when the body differs; skipped in a dry run).

```
notme issue-body N|REF --body-file F
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `N|REF` | required | a number (in the tracker), #N, owner/name#N or a URL |
| `--body-file F` | required |  |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, number, updated

### `notme followup`

Create a follow-up issue in the tracker, or in --repo when given (the allow list decides whether that repo may be written); --parent also ticks it into that issue's task list, which must be in the same repo.

```

```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--title-file F` | required |  |
| `--body-file F` | required |  |
| `--source N` | optional |  |
| `--parent N` | optional |  |
| `--labels a,b` | optional |  |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: number, url (both null in a dry run), parent

### `notme retro save`


| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--run-id RID` | required |  |
| `--audit-file F` | required |  |
| `--reviewed` | optional | also mark the run as reviewed |

### `notme allow-repo add`

Allow a repo (or, with --board, a project board) for this project or everywhere. Only a person may do this: it must run from a terminal Claude Code did not start and be given the operator token (typed at a hidden prompt, or in NOT_ME_OPERATOR_CONFIRM for scripts); otherwise the refusal (kind human_only) carries the command to run. The guard is the enforcement; this check is a second layer.

```
notme allow-repo add SLUG [--board OWNER/NUMBER] [--everywhere]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `SLUG` | optional |  |
| `--board OWNER/NUMBER` | optional |  |
| `--everywhere` | optional | for every project, not only this one |

Output: added, scope, repo or board

### `notme allow-repo remove`

Remove a repo (or --board) from the allow list. The same person check as add applies.

```
notme allow-repo remove SLUG [--board OWNER/NUMBER] [--everywhere]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `SLUG` | optional |  |
| `--board OWNER/NUMBER` | optional |  |
| `--everywhere` | optional | for every project, not only this one |

Output: removed, scope, repo or board

### `notme allow-repo list`

The allow list entries for this project and the global ones.

```
notme allow-repo list
```

Output: entries (scope, repo or board, added)

### `notme git unstash`

Apply a stash by sha and drop it.

```

```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `SHA` | required |  |

Output: restored

### `notme git worktree-add`

Add a detached worktree at a sha. PATH must be below <git-common-dir>/not-me/worktrees/.

```
notme git worktree-add PATH SHA
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `PATH` | required |  |
| `SHA` | required |  |

Output: path, sha

### `notme git worktree-remove`

Remove a worktree.

```
notme git worktree-remove PATH
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `PATH` | required |  |

Output: path, removed

### `notme git remote-branch-exists`

Whether origin has the branch (git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin NAME), and its sha.

```
notme git remote-branch-exists NAME
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `NAME` | required |  |

Output: exists, sha (null when it does not exist)

### `notme git status`

The checkout's branch, cleanliness and origin repo.

```
notme git status
```

Output: branch, clean, default_branch, origin

### `notme status`

A read-only summary: enabled and paused state, the active run, items needing a person, stale claims, and the last run of each skill. When GitHub cannot be read the items are left out with a warning. Creates nothing.

```
notme status
```

Output: enabled, paused (global, project), mode, repo, tracker, operator, active_run, items, stale_claims, last_runs, warnings

### `notme pause`

Turn not-me off or on for this project (or for every project with --global) by writing or removing the PAUSED file. Pick and claim commands then report paused. `pause off` needs the same person check as allow-repo add (else kind human_only, with the command for a person to run).

```
notme pause state [--global]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `state {on|off}` | required |  |
| `--global` | optional | for every project |

Output: paused, scope

### `notme mode show`

The effective mode, the layer, file and line it comes from, what the global and repo layers each say, and whether the repo layer pins dry-run (repo_pin: path, file, line). dry_run also counts --dry-run and NOT_ME_DRY_RUN. A global `mode: live` counts only when signed: live_confirmed says whether the marker that `notme mode live` writes (<not-me home>/mode-live.sig, an HMAC keyed by the operator token and the epoch) verifies; when the layers say live but it does not, mode is dry-run and unconfirmed holds the warning (else null). token_present says whether the operator token file exists; launcher is the absolute path of this notme, and live_cmd the command a person runs in their own terminal to go live, written for shell: posix, or git-bash on Windows (bin/notme is a bash script, so not PowerShell or cmd). Neither the token nor the marker is shown.

```
notme mode show
```

Output: mode, dry_run, source (layer, path, line[, ignored, downgraded]), layers (global, repo: mode, path, line, file), repo_pin, live_confirmed, unconfirmed, token_present, launcher, shell, live_cmd

### `notme mode dry-run`

Set `mode: dry-run` in the repo layer (<project>/.claude/not-me/project.md), or with --global in the global layer (<not-me home>/project.md), which also deletes the live marker and replaces the epoch (<not-me home>/mode-live.epoch), so no saved copy of an old marker verifies again (the repo layer leaves both). Always allowed: it only tightens. A missing or empty file gets minimal frontmatter; otherwise only the mode line changes. Kind mode_edit_refused when the file cannot be edited safely: text without frontmatter, frontmatter that does not parse, a symlink or hard link in the repo layer, or a global symlink that does not lead to a regular project.md.

```
notme mode dry-run [--global]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--global` | optional | in the global layer, not the repo layer |

Output: the mode show keys, plus written (layer, file, mode)

### `notme mode live`

Set `mode: live` in the global layer only (the repo layer can never turn live mode on) and sign it: write <not-me home>/mode-live.sig, an HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the operator token and the epoch in <not-me home>/mode-live.epoch (created when missing), without which `mode: live` runs as dry-run. Only a person may do this, with the same check as allow-repo add (else kind human_only, with the command to run). After a token rotation, run it again. When the repo layer still pins dry-run, the global layer is written anyway and repo_pin names that file and line.

```
notme mode live
```

Output: the mode show keys, plus written (layer, file, mode) and, when the repo pins dry-run, note

### `notme doctor`

Check the tools and setup: python, git and gh versions, config, mode (a warning when `mode: live` is set but not confirmed by `notme mode live`), gh auth and scopes, guard self-test, spawn depth. Exit 7 when the only failed required checks are gh, gh auth or gh scopes; exit 1 when another required check fails. --init-token instead creates <not-me home>/operator-token (random, mode 0600) and shows it once; only a person may run it (kind human_only otherwise), and an existing token is never replaced (kind token_exists: delete the file to make a new one).

```
notme doctor [--init-token]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--init-token` | optional | create the operator token (a person only; shown once) |

Output: ok, checks (name, ok, detail, required); with --init-token token, path
